newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate down on weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate down on weak demand.

text.p: Croatia's money market rate edged down to 9.3 percent from 11.1 percent on Thursday, weighed by dwindling demand for kuna funds.
Total settlements further shrank to 10.7 million kuna against supply of 75 million.
Dealers said there was no demand for fresh kuna loans, as there were more than 500 million kuna on banks' giro-accounts for the third day in a row, boosting the money supply.

Insurers rolled over previous short-term loans at a steady 8.0-percent rate. The state bank HBOR rolled over previous loans at 12 percent, bosting the average call money rate to 10.8 from 9.7 percent.
There was no overnight trade as no banks reported shortfalls.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday slightly fimer to 5.4112 against the dollar and 3.5628 versus the mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
